answer.rationale: Finance's 18% cut is non-negotiable and the incumbent has closed the door on price, so renewal, renegotiation, and deferral all fail the primary objective. Memory c2 is the only record that speaks directly to the path we must take: shifting primary supply to the lower-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply and onboarding was quick, with accurate invoicing. I want to verify that record because the assembly line is at 94% with no buffer, so I need confidence the c2 onboarding speed was real and not an artifact of a slower production period. If the archive confirms quick onboarding and clean invoicing, we issue a 60-day primary-supply award to the low-cost vendor, overlapping the final two weeks of the incumbent contract so the switch is seamless. We deliberately skip a multi-year term (memory c6) this cycle to preserve flexibility while the new vendor proves itself, and we log a follow-up for next review to add a second source for the constrained component (memory c3) once the primary transition is stable.
